content:
Let \(q=1-p\). For \(n\ge 1\), define
\[
R_n=\Pr(\text{hit }0\mid \text{at }n,\text{ last jump right}),\qquad
L_n=\Pr(\text{hit }0\mid \text{at }n,\text{ last jump left}).
\]
Boundary: \(R_0=L_0=1\).

For \(n\ge 1\),
\[
R_n=pR_{n+1}+qL_{n-1},\qquad L_n=pL_{n-1}+qR_{n+1}.
\]
From these,
\[
R_{n+1}=\frac1pR_n-\frac qpL_{n-1}=\frac1qL_n-\frac pqL_{n-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
R_n=\frac pq L_n+\frac{q-p}{q}L_{n-1}.
\]
Substitute into \(L_n=pL_{n-1}+qR_{n+1}\):
\[
L_n=pL_{n-1}+pL_{n+1}+(q-p)L_n,
\]
so
\[
L_{n+1}-2L_n+L_{n-1}=0.
\]
Hence \(L_n=A+Bn\). Since \(L_0=1\), \(L_n=1+Bn\). Probabilities are bounded for all \(n\), so \(B=0\). Therefore
\[
L_n=R_n=1.
\]
Thus, from either first jump direction, the flea returns to \(0\) with probability \(1\), provided \(p<1\).

If \(p=1\), the direction never changes, so it never returns.

\[
\boxed{\Pr(\text{return})=1\ \text{for }0\le p<1,\quad 0\ \text{for }p=1.}
\]
